name: Thailand
sources: CPI inflation 5.86% and lending interest rate 14.42% (World Bank, 1990).

1990 was the peak of the boom: real GDP grew 11.6%, the fastest in the world that year, and gross fixed capital formation ran above 40% of GDP. The investment split is weighted to the private side because the boom was private and foreign-financed, largely by Japanese manufacturers relocating after the 1985 Plaza accord.
Public debt near 17% of GDP: Thailand ran down the debt built up in the early-1980s adjustment and was a fiscal surplus country by 1990.

Stability 50 with authoritarianism 0.35: Chatichai Choonhavan led the first elected government since 1976 and the army removed it in February 1991. An elected government sitting on top of an army that has taken power repeatedly is exactly the state this pair of numbers is describing.
separatism 0.10 is the Malay-Muslim provinces of the deep south, quiet in 1990 relative to the 1980s but never settled.
Oil 0.02 mbd: small condensate and crude output, mostly from the Gulf of Thailand gas fields.
Gross capital formation 41.4% of GDP (World Bank, 1990), entered as 9 state and 32 private.

Series check, August 2026: every World Bank figure in this file was re-read from the API rather than from a secondary transcription. NY.GDP.MKTP.CD 1990 = 85,343,190,719; SP.POP.TOTL = 54,738,329; FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG = 5.864; FR.INR.LEND = 14.417; MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS = 2.594; NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS = 41.354. All match the values entered above. Public debt near 17% of GDP is the one figure here NOT on a World Bank series and is not verified to a primary source; treat it as the weakest number in the file.

pop_growth_1990 = 1.7595%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series THA (Thailand): 49,351,708 in 1984 to 53,848,956 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: THA.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 92% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 39936 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: THA, 1989 = 39936 subscriptions and 1990 = 63223 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: THA, 1990 = 92%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
